dossier.public_summary: The dip does not come from the target star. Difference imaging puts it about 39 arcseconds away, offset by 35 sigma. The same signal changes depth by a factor of two between sectors and matches a nearby faint star 44 arcseconds away that needs only a 1.7% eclipse. Together this is a blended eclipsing binary, not a planet on the target.

reasons.why: difference imaging puts the dip ~39 arcsec west of the target at >30 sigma. on_target=off is direct positive evidence the dip is not on the target, favouring a blended binary over a planet on target.
reasons.value: verdict=off_target offset_arcsec=38.94 (39.422699000563966 in centroid_all) offset_sigma=35.77 (31.48680664023439) sectors_used=1 (2 in centroid_all)

reasons.why: the nearest star bright enough to cause the dip is 43.6 arcsec away needing only a 1.7% eclipse and lies 3-4 sigma from the measured centroid. It is plausibly the source and is much closer than any other suspect (67.3 arcsec needed 0.0899), explaining an off-target blend.

depth doubles across sectors with the same TESS-SPOC aperture code. sector_depths_by_source verdict=changes_within_a_source p_constant=0.00016255164122965158 so depth is not a per-source calibration. A planet on target must have steady depth within a product; a factor ~2 change is expected from a varying relative contribution of a neighbour in different pointings/apertures.
reasons.value: p_constant=0.0001627 per_sector: 1658±662 ppm (sec 42), 4321±637 ppm (sec 43), 5486±671 ppm (sec 70) depth_change_pct=100.2

reasons.why: no star could cause the dip inside one TESS pixel (21 arcsec), but 11 could do so with deeper eclipses. The could_cause at 43.6 arcsec provides the exact position, consistent with centroid being outside the target pixel but still in the aperture wings.

large spot variability at the transit period in one sector supports the dip is tied to the local stellar light (blended/spot) rather than a quiet target star; flat-bottom shape v_sigma=-1.657 alone cannot overcome the centroid offset evidence.
